notes: Rooms: the National Gallery of Art's own outlines for every public room of the West Building's Main and Ground Floors (its open data, CC0), put into metres at 0.44385 m a map pixel with the Rotunda's centre on the model's dome; each room keeps the NGA's words for it. Where the NGA gives a gallery and its parts (73 and 73A, 73B; 42 and 42A-D) the parts are drawn; outlines that overlap by a pixel or two are parted down the middle; identical outlines under several keys (Gallery 1 and 1A-1C, the Founder's Room and its alcove, the West Stair Lobby and Landing, Gallery 26 and 26A) are one room known by all. The way in: the Sixth Street door on Constitution Avenue into the North Lobby (the NGA's three parts of it drawn as one space, no wall between), its two stairs up to the North Stair Landings; on the Main Floor, the rotunda's passages to the two sculpture halls (Wikipedia). Which other rooms connect is not known yet: the NGA's visitor map is the source for that, and www.nga.gov refuses a session, as does the Internet Archive's file store for its 2022 campus map guide; so every gallery is drawn and its works hung, but it has no way in known yet: a gallery that holds saved works is come into by a cut, with no doorway drawn, and the walk says so ('no way in is known yet · placed here'). The two floors' levels and every height are the model's; no finish is published in a source read yet. The wings' outer galleries lie beyond the model's wings, which are too shallow: a finding for the model.¶ The site's hanging beside the known (INTERIORS.md, 'Beside the known'): the works the National Gallery of Art holds that its records do not place in a room drawn here are hung by the site beside the works its records place — 188 in the first room from the door with wall free.
